findings.source_quote: "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people."
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the entire quoted sentence into Afrikaans, preserving it as a quotation and keeping surrounding HTML tags unchanged. For example: "Ek het die opdrag ontvang van die koninklike en prinslike Meester, my Here Jesus, om Christus aan die volk te preek."
findings.translation_quote: "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people."

findings.location: Paragraph beginning "My removal from my flock is so heavy..." (source.html) — quoted sentence
findings.source_quote: "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the full quotation into Afrikaans, keeping it as a single quoted passage and preserving HTML. Example: "My verwydering van my kudde is so swaar vir my, dat dit my lewe 'n las maak; ek het nog nooit so 'n verlange na die dood gehad nie. Die Here help en hou hierdie droewe klei op."
findings.translation_quote: "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."

findings.location: Paragraph beginning "Rutherford continued to be an influential leader..." (source.html) — quoted summons sentence
findings.source_quote: "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the quotation into Afrikaans, preserving it as a quotation. Example: "Ek het reeds 'n dagvaarding van 'n hoër Regter, en ek behoort my eerste dagvaarding te beantwoord; en wanneer julle dag aanbreek, sal ek wees waar min konings en grootmense kom."
findings.translation_quote: "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."

findings.location: Hymn stanza 4 (The Lamb with His fair army...)
findings.source_quote: "The Lamb with His fair army, Doth on Mount Zion stand;"
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the Afrikaans to reflect the original meaning "fair army" (i.e., a noble/beautiful host), not a fearful or terrible army. For example: "Die Lam met Sy lieflike leër, Staan op Sion se berg;" (or "Die Lam met Sy pragtige leër"). Preserve the stanza HTML and formatting.
findings.translation_quote: "Die Lam met Sy vreeslike leër, Staan op Sion se berg;"

findings.location: Hymn stanza 1, line 3 ("The summer morn I’ve sighed for")
findings.suggested_fix: Adjust the Afrikaans verb to 'gesug het' (sighed) rather than 'gesuig het' (sucked). Example: "Die somermôre waarna ek gesug het," Preserve stanza tags and emphasis.

findings.location: Paragraph about the tune (near end) — refrain left in English
findings.suggested_fix: Either translate the quoted refrain into Afrikaans in that narrative sentence or place a parallel translated version in parentheses right after the English refrain, to reflect the printed English while giving an Afrikaans rendering. Example: "... die refrein—'En heerlikheid, heerlikheid woon in Immanuel se land.'"
findings.translation_quote: "And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

findings.location: Final paragraph — closing quote left in English
findings.suggested_fix: Translate this closing quotation into Afrikaans while preserving it as a quotation. Example: "Hulle verloor niks wat Christus gewen het nie."
